> Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $r(x)$ be the smallest even integer $t$ such that $d_n = t$ has no solutions for $n \le x$. Is it true that $r(x) / \log x \to \infty$?
